name: Lat Pulldown Machine
setup: Adjust the thigh pad snugly over your thighs so your body doesn't lift off the seat. Select a manageable weight pin.
how_to_use: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width, lean back slightly, and pull the bar down to your upper chest while squeezing your shoulder blades together. Return slowly with control.
safety: Never pull the bar behind your neck (stresses the shoulders). Avoid swinging your lower back to jerk heavy weight.

name: Leg Press Machine
setup: Sit with your back and hips flat against the pad. Place feet shoulder-width apart on the middle of the sled. Release the side safety handles after extending slightly.
how_to_use: Lower the sled slowly until your knees reach ~90 degrees, then push through your mid-foot and heels back up without locking your knees.
safety: NEVER lock your knees at the top, and do not let your lower back curl off the seat at the bottom. Always re-engage the safety latches before letting go.

name: Chest Press Machine
setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles line up with your mid-chest. Keep your shoulder blades retracted against the backrest.
how_to_use: Push the handles forward until your arms are almost straight, pause briefly, and return slowly without letting the weight stack slam.
safety: Keep elbows slightly below shoulder height (~45 degrees) to protect your shoulder joints.

name: Cable Crossover / Functional Trainer
setup: Set the pulley height (high for triceps pushdowns/face pulls, chest height for cable flies/Pallof press, low for curls/rows) and clip on the desired attachment (rope, straight bar, D-handle).
how_to_use: Step away slightly to create tension before starting the set, keep your core braced, and control both the pull and return phases.
safety: Check that the carabiner is fully closed and the weight pin is pushed all the way in before pulling.

name: Smith Machine
setup: Set the lower safety stops at the bottom of your range of motion. Twist the bar forward/back to unhook it from the catches.
how_to_use: Used for squats, incline presses, lunges, or calf raises along a fixed vertical rail. For squats, place your feet slightly in front of the bar.
safety: Always set the safety stoppers before lifting heavy, and verify the hooks are fully locked back onto the pegs before letting go.

name: Squat Rack / Power Cage
setup: Set J-hooks at mid-chest height (for squats/OHP) and set the safety bars/straps just below the bottom of your squat.
how_to_use: Always unrack by stepping backwards into the rack so you walk forward to rerack safely when fatigued.
safety: Always use barbell collars/clips to keep weight plates from sliding off, and never squat heavy without safety bars.

name: Olympic Barbell & Weight Plates
setup: Standard Olympic bars weigh 20 kg (45 lb). Load plates evenly on both sides and secure them with collars.
how_to_use: Used for compound lifts: bench press, back squat, deadlift, barbell row, overhead press, and Romanian deadlift.
safety: Learn technique with an empty bar first; keep a neutral spine on deadlifts and rows.

name: Dumbbells
setup: Pick a pair you can lift for 8-12 reps with clean form. Stand back from the dumbbell rack so others can access weights.
how_to_use: Versatile for pressing, rowing, curling, lateral raises, goblet squats, lunges, and Romanian deadlifts.
safety: Lift dumbbells off the floor with a flat back and bent knees; lower them gently instead of dropping them.

name: Kettlebell
setup: Check that you have clear floor space around you and grip the handle firmly with chalk or dry hands.
how_to_use: Ideal for goblet squats, kettlebell swings (hip hinge, not a squat), deadlifts, and farmer's carries.
safety: On swings, drive power from the hips and glutes—never round or hyperextend your lower back.

name: Leg Curl / Leg Extension Machine
setup: Align the machine's pivot point with your knee joint. Adjust the ankle pad so it rests just above your heels (curl) or on the lower shin (extension).
how_to_use: Move smoothly through a full range of motion, pause 1 second at peak contraction, and lower slowly.
safety: Do not kick or swing the weight; stop if you feel sharp knee joint pain.

name: Adjustable Weight Bench
setup: Lock the backrest pin securely into flat (0°), incline (30-45°), or upright (75-85°) position and test it with your hand before lying down.
how_to_use: Supports dumbbell/barbell presses, one-arm dumbbell rows, Bulgarian split squats, bench dips, and hip thrusts.
safety: Always check that the adjustment pin is fully seated in its slot before loading weight.

name: Pec Deck / Chest Fly & Rear Delt Machine
setup: Adjust seat height so handles align with mid-chest. Set the arm range-of-motion pin so you feel a comfortable stretch without shoulder strain.
how_to_use: With a slight bend in the elbows, bring the handles together in front of your chest, squeeze, and return slowly. Face the backrest with arms set forward for rear delts.
safety: Don't let the arms swing too far behind your torso; protect the front of the shoulder.

name: Pull-Up / Dip Station (Power Tower)
setup: If using an assisted machine, remember MORE weight on the pin makes the exercise EASIER (more counterweight).
how_to_use: Supports pull-ups, chin-ups, parallel-bar dips, and hanging leg raises.
safety: Control the descent on dips; don't drop your shoulders below elbow level if you feel shoulder discomfort.

name: Treadmill
setup: Stand on the side rails before starting the belt. Clip the red safety stop key to your shirt.
how_to_use: Great for 5-10 min warm-ups, brisk incline walking (e.g., 5-10% incline at 4.5-5.5 km/h for fat loss), or running intervals.
safety: Avoid holding the front handrails while walking at steep inclines—lower the incline instead so you keep natural posture.

name: Rowing Machine (Ergometer)
setup: Set the damper to 3-5 (not 10!). Strap your feet securely across the widest part of the foot.
how_to_use: Follow the sequence: Legs push → slight torso lean back → Arms pull to lower ribs. Return in reverse: Arms → Torso → Legs.
safety: Keep your back flat (don't slump at the catch) and drive primarily with your legs, not just your arms.
